method.grain: one row per player; season values aggregated by PA/BF/BBE weight before binning
method.grade_binning: nearest 5, clipped to [20, 80]; grade_mean carries the unrounded bin centre

notes: MLB context. BBE-weighted across all MLB seasons, 50 BBE floor per season. No published outlet band exists in EV units.

published_notes: BA publishes only the starter table plus 'add 1-2 mph for relievers'; the BA reliever row here is the starter band plus 1 to 2 mph.

hr_per600_career.published_unit: home runs per full MLB season (600 PA)

hr_per600_fullseason.published_unit: home runs per full MLB season (600 PA)

hr_per600_age26.published_unit: home runs per full MLB season (600 PA)

bb_pct_sp.published_unit: MLB walk rate, percent, starters (lower is better)

bb_pct_rp.published_unit: MLB walk rate, percent, relievers (lower is better)

fielding_runs.published_unit: defensive runs per full MLB season

_published.lefty: FanGraphs (Smith W2) and Baseball America both prescribe subtracting 1 mph from every velocity threshold for left-handers, i.e. LHP measured velocity should sit about 1 mph BELOW RHP at the same grade.
_published.reliever: Baseball America prescribes adding 1 to 2 mph for relievers; Smith W2's published reliever table sits 1 to 3 mph above his starter table. Both imply RP measured velocity should sit 1 to 2 mph ABOVE SP at the same grade.
_published.caveat: Our role split is REALIZED MLB usage (career GS/G), not the role the grade was written for, so most of our RP group are prospects scouted as starters who ended up in relief. That population is velocity-selected downward relative to a scouted reliever, and the contrast should be read as a lower bound on the true role adjustment.

raw_pwr.verdict: NOT COMPUTABLE (fewer than two sources above floor)

raw_pwr@aaa.verdict: NOT COMPUTABLE (fewer than two sources above floor)

_baseballamerica.reason: Baseball America contributes rank and FV to this tree but no tool grades at all: zero BA tool rows across the whole snapshot history. A BA drift index cannot be computed, so BA's published bands can only be audited against our measurements, never against BA's own grades.

no_measurement.throw: No arm-strength observation exists anywhere in this tree: no throw velocity, no catcher pop time, no outfield assist-runs split. Baseball America's catcher pop-time table is the only published arm scale in measured units and it is unauditable here.
no_measurement.pitch_sel: No plate-discipline decomposition is joined at the player-season grain in either context; BB% is a consequence, not the tool.
no_measurement.bat_ctrl: No bat tracking for the minors (bat_speed and swing_length are present as columns in the savant minors export and empty in every row) and no MLB bat-tracking join keyed to prospect grades.
no_measurement.delivery: Not a measured quantity; arm angle and extension exist in data/aaa_physics.json but neither is what the grade names.
no_measurement.frame: Height and weight exist as FanGraphs extras; the grade is not a height-weight function and no body-composition measurement exists.
no_measurement.speed_run_time: PARTIAL. No sprint speed, no 60-yard time, no home-to-first time anywhere in the tree, so both published speed tables (seconds) are unauditable. Stolen bases and triples are outcome proxies and are reported as proxies.
